For example, a young person who is looking to aggressively grow their retirement savings (since they have a lot of time to ride out the stock market highs and lows) might gravitate toward [growth stocks](https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/learn/best-performing-growth-stocks) for their high-risk, high-reward volatility. The other rule of thumb, which is more conservative, and better for hands-off or beginner investors, is to invest no more than 10% of your portfolio in individual stocks overall, and leave the other 90% in [index funds](https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/learn/how-to-invest-in-index-funds). For more information on brokers that are working to make stock trading more accessible, check out our roundup of the [best brokers for beginners](https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/best/online-brokers-for-beginners). By Chris Davis](https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/best/online-brokers-for-stock-trading).

There are many ways to invest — from safe choices such as high-yield savings accounts and CDs to medium-risk options such as [corporate bonds](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/corporate-bonds/) to higher-risk investments such as stock index funds. [Corporate bond funds can be an excellent choice](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/how-to-invest-in-bonds/) for investors looking for cash flow, such as retirees, or those who want to reduce their overall portfolio risk but still earn a return. [Dividend stock funds](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/best-dividend-etfs/) are a good investment for almost any kind of stock investor, but they're ideal for those looking for income. Small-cap stock funds can earn sizable returns over time, and the [best small-cap ETFs](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/best-etfs/) can earn double-digit returns annually for years. An S&P 500 index fund is an [excellent choice for beginning investors](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/best-investments-for-beginners/) because it provides broad, diversified exposure to the stock market. An S&P 500 fund is one of the less-risky ways to [invest in stocks](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/how-to-invest-in-stocks/), because it’s made up of the market’s top companies and is highly diversified.
